rules.description: A deep, green-tinted black acting as the primary text ink and anchoring highly technical sections with dark backgrounds.
when_to_use: Main body and heading typography throughout the page
Technical diagram and evaluation section backgrounds ('#001C17', '#001A16')

rules.description: A comprehensive suite of whites and off-whites that structure the layout, delineate content, and provide soft contrast.
when_to_use: Primary feature cards and sticky header backgrounds ('#FFFFFF')
Default page and hero section containers ('#F8F7F5', '#F3F3F3')
Interactive text input fields and file upload zones ('#F3F3F3')
Subtle dividers and borders on interactive elements ('#E5E7EB', '#D1D5DB')

rules.description: Absolute black applied selectively for maximum contrast, primarily isolating the blog content from the core product UI.
when_to_use: Article titles, author names, and metadata in the blog carousel
Category pill borders on blog cards
Subtle drop shadows on 'How it works' instructional cards

rules.description: A muted secondary ink providing visual hierarchy for supporting information and deactivated states.
when_to_use: Model manufacturer labels in benchmark cards (e.g., Anthropic, OpenAI)
Instructional microcopy like 'Try an example' and 'Try a sample image'

rules.description: The vibrant brand accent driving core conversions, scaling down into rich espresso browns for premium feature cards.
when_to_use: Primary 'Try It for Free' and 'Contact Sales' button backgrounds
Highlighted step numbers and accent typography (e.g., 'Global Brands')
Enterprise solution and plagiarism feature card backgrounds ('#562301', '#612700')

insights: The design leverages a stark contrast between airy, off-white layouts and dense, ultra-dark technical sections, balancing approachable product marketing with rigorous scientific authority.
Rather than defaulting to neutral grays for dark mode components, the brand commits to deep forest greens and espresso browns, embedding an earthy, academic mood directly into the UI.
Vibrant orange is used sparingly but effectively, cutting through both pure white surfaces and dark environments to guarantee high visibility for primary actions and data points.
